channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Investors Patient With IPO Plan
item.description: CEO Sam Altman says OpenAI ultimately wants to become a public company, but not yet. Speaking with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg The Close," Altman pushes back on the idea that the responsibilities of being public are incompatible with a focus on safety. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Altman Says OpenAI Investors Patient on IPO Amid Safety Focus
item.description: OpenAI’s Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said the company wants to navigate a period of heightened artificial intelligence safety concerns without the pressure of being a newly public company and believes investors will be “patient” with its IPO planning.
item.dc:creator: Seth Fiegerman and Ed Ludlow

item.title: OpenAI Will Keep Driving Down Prices, Sam Altman Says
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says the company wants to keep driving down the price of artificial intelligence. He talks about the launch of their new AI agent called Dots with Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow at the company's annual developer conference in San Francisco. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
item.description: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent weeks, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.
item.dc:creator: William Norris, Nilushi Karunaratne and Thomas Pfeiffer

item.title: Trump Hosts AI Leaders at White House
item.description: Artificial intelligence industry leaders met with President Donald Trump to discuss growing concerns over threats posed by the technology. Trump has said he doesn't want to stifle innovation by using too much regulation. Palantir Technologies CEO Alex Karp was among those at the meeting and he spoke to Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Citi, Coinbase Team Up To Let Merchants Accept Stablecoins
item.description: Bloomberg's Anna Irrera joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Citigroup is partnering with Coinbase Global to allow the bank’s institutional clients to accept stablecoin payments, as large financial institutions step up their involvement in new forms of digital money. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Holds Back Astra Model Over Safety Concerns
item.description: OpenAI is holding back a version of its advanced Astra model while it develops stronger safeguards, offering one of the clearest examples yet of what the company’s call for “pacing” AI development means in practice. Bloomberg’s Natasha Mascarenhas discusses concerns that the model wasn’t reliably staying within its authorized scope, and recent incidents involving OpenAI models accessing outside systems. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SEC Has 'Turned Corner' On Crypto: Hester Peirce
item.description: SEC commissioner, Hester Peirce joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." This week marks the last week for Peirce as a commissioner of the SEC. They discuss how the crypto industry has changed in her almost nine years as commissioner. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s AI Push Meets a More Cautious Silicon Valley
item.description: Council on Foreign Relations senior fellow Sebastian Mallaby discusses the Trump administration’s push to use AI to make the federal government more accessible and efficient, while navigating a growing divide over how quickly the technology should advance. He also examines the evolving relationship between President Trump and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, whose warnings about AI risk contrast with the administration’s focus on accelerating US development and maintaining its lead over China. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We Care About Scale, Liquidity: BofA's Theisen
item.description: Sonali Theisen, global head of digital assets platform, FICC e-trading, and markets strategy investments at Bank of America, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dyson Blames ‘Water Seepage’ for Rocky Debut of $499 AI Toothbrush
item.description: Dyson Ltd. said water seepage caused an early batch of its new artificial intelligence-powered toothbrushes to malfunction, offering its first explanation for the product’s disappearance from stores.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Murphy Kelly

item.title: Flows Stabilizing: Bitget CEO Discusses Crypto Hack
item.description: Gracy Chen, BitGet CEO, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." Hacked crypto exchange Bitget recorded roughly $463 million in net outflows in the 24 hours into Tuesday, as customers moved assets off the platform following last week’s $388 million theft. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AMD Goes Big on World Models as Anthropic Heads to IPO
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down President Trump's new AI-powered website America.gov, putting AI at the center of his agenda. Plus, Anthropic warns of "existential risks to humanity" in its prospectus ahead of its IPO according to reports, and AMD makes a big AI bet on the frontier by acquiring Fei-Fei Li's World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at $8.2 billion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hypertec on AI Infrastructure Investment
item.description: Simon Ahdoot, CEO, Hypertec, discusses how the growth of AI and cloud computing is driving demand for hyperscale data centers, where constraints could emerge and what Canada needs to compete for AI infrastructure investment, with Bloomberg’s Mathieu Dion at the 2026 Bloomberg Canadian Finance Conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ternus busca transformar Apple para competir en era de IA
item.description: Menos capas gerenciales y más contacto entre ingenieros y altos ejecutivos. El sucesor de Tim Cook empieza a reestructurar Apple con la mira puesta en acelerar lanzamientos y reducir la burocracia.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: OpenAI Targets $30 Billion in New Funding at $1.4 Trillion Value
item.description: OpenAI aims to raise at least $30 billion from investors in a new round of funding, according to people familiar with the matter, after the artificial intelligence startup pushed back its plans for an initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence, Ed Ludlow and Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: How the Rise of Prediction Markets Impacts Sportsbooks
item.description: Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick reports on how the rise of prediction markets is impacting sports betting and if more regulation is needed. Executives from BetMGM, DraftKings, FanDuel, Robinhood and Fanatics all weigh in. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Unveils Always-On AI Agent Dots, New $500 Paid Tier
item.description: OpenAI has unveiled an always-on artificial intelligence agent that’s designed to proactively tackle work on a user’s behalf, competing with firms like Meta Platforms Inc. in a growing field for AI-powered digital assistants.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz

item.title: Data Centers Spell $3 Billion Opportunity for Catering Firms
item.description: Catering companies have a $3 billion opportunity: providing food, gyms and entertainment to a growing cohort of data center workers.
item.dc:creator: Chloé Meley and Ann Gehan

item.title: What El Niño Could Cost Africa | Bloomberg Next Africa
item.description: In this edition of Next Africa, we examine the economic risks from El Niño as drought and floods threaten crops, food prices and hydropower across the continent. Jennifer Zabasajja speaks with experts about the regions most exposed, the investment needed to strengthen Africa's water resilience and how AI tools are helping smallholder farmers make critical decisions as weather becomes harder to predict. (Corrects onscreen figure to reflect $6.7T financing gap.) (Source: Bloomberg)
